title: Operational blame matrix and retry heuristics dashboard for inference errors
creator: Asha Patel
description: Background: Production inference traffic exhibits several recurring error modes (client timeouts, overload-triggered rejects, model rejections/tokenization failures, and various HTTP/gRPC status mappings). Current dashboards show high-level error rates but lack a systematic way to attribute issues to route, model variant, or infrastructure layer. Goal: deliver a dashboard + taxonomy that surfaces the dominant operational contributors to user-facing failures and produces actionable retry/circuit-breaker guidance for downstream services. This ticket covers taxonomy design, runtime span tagging changes, enrichment in the metrics/log pipeline, Grafana panel set, alert rules, and an on-call playbook update.
work_items: Draft failure taxonomy and retryability matrix (timeouts, overload, model_error, client_abort, grpc/HTTP status mapping)
Define span and log field contract: error_class, error_subtype, model_id, route, backend_queue_ms, kv_cache_hit
Instrument serving runtime to emit error_class tags and queue/backpressure metrics
Pipeline ETL: map logs to taxonomy, enrich traces, forward derived metrics to Prometheus and long-term aggregates to BigQuery
Build Grafana dashboard: blame matrix heatmap, per-route error breakdown, p50/p95 latency slices, retryability guidance panel, and synthetic probe overlay
Create alert rules and automated runbook links for high-impact cells in the blame matrix
Run a 2-week shadow rollout and compare with historical incidents to validate coverage
decisions: Use a unified "error_class" field at the trace/span/log level with canonical values: timeout, overload, model_error, client_error, network_error, internal_error
Map gRPC codes to canonical classes (UNAVAILABLE -> network_error, RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED -> overload, INVALID_ARGUMENT -> client_error)
Dynamic trace sampling: baseline 1% for all requests, 100% sampling for traces with error_class != null and 10% for routes with recent SLO breaches
Metrics model: emit per-route per-model counters for error_class and latency histogram buckets to Prometheus; rollups to BigQuery for 90-day queries

Retry heuristic: classify errors as retryable/non-retryable in taxonomy. Default client guidance: retry on transient network_error and UNAVAILABLE with exponential backoff up to 3 attempts; do not retry model_error or INVALID_ARGUMENT
Dashboard tech: Grafana + Tempo for traces, Prometheus for metrics, BigQuery for trend analysis; store enriched logs in OpenSearch for ad-hoc queries
progress_updates: 2025-01-12: PRD and first-pass taxonomy posted to Confluence (see artifacts)
2025-01-20: prototype heatmap panel implemented in staging Grafana using synthetic logs
2025-02-02: runtime instrumentation PR opened (github.com/redwood-inference/serving/pull/2345) to add error_class span tag and backend_queue_ms metric
2025-02-10: ingestion pipeline changes merged (github.com/redwood-inference/observability/pull/345) to map gRPC/HTTP codes to canonical classes and emit per-route counters
2025-02-16: Grafana dashboard complete in staging, awaiting SRE and PM review; playbook draft under review
acceptance_criteria: Taxonomy document reviewed and approved by PM, SRE, and runtime owners
Serving runtime emits error_class and backend_queue_ms for >= 95% of traffic in canary region
Grafana dashboard (blame matrix + retry guidance) available in staging with drill-down to Tempo traces
Alert rules created for high-severity cells and integrated with on-call Slack/PagerDuty runbooks
Shadow rollout shows taxonomy covers >= 90% of historical incidents from the last 60 days or items added to taxonomy list
notes: Trade-offs: adding error_class at the span level increases trace size; to control cost we rely on dynamic sampling and selective 100% sampling for error traces.
Edge cases: some model rejections are ambiguous (e.g., low confidence vs. toxic content); these will be captured under model_error.subtype and reviewed during the shadow run.
Follow-ups: consider adding GPU preemption and OOM counters to the blame matrix in a follow-up ticket if infrastructure-related cells surface as significant contributors.
